clue.text: Dizzy blonde?

blocks.note: first meaning: faint and giddy
second meaning, read literally: having fair, pale-coloured hair on top

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dizzy blonde' reads as a tired stereotype, but the two words are separate meanings; the question mark flags the literal reading of fair hair on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Giddiness and a pale head of hair are both described by the same hyphenated adjective, one figurative and one literal.

clue.text: Servant, 13, with day off

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the answer to 13 across
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy servant is having a day off work.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 13 is used for its answer, not its clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady's maid is a personal female attendant in a household, a classic domestic servant role.

clue.text: Old woman, awfully angry, penning note

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out jumbled
to pen something is to enclose it, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
N is a standard abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: An old woman, furious, is writing a note.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny is a grandmother, used informally of any elderly woman.

clue.text: Lawrence of Arabia's birthplace - Democrat misdirected

indicators.note: something misdirected is sent the wrong way, so the letters go into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Democrat has been sent the wrong way when looking for where T. E. Lawrence was born.
explanation.walkthrough: Tremadoc (now Tremadog) is a village in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: T. E. Lawrence, known as Lawrence of Arabia, was born in 1888 in the Welsh village of Tremadoc.

clue.text: Girl's TV awards

blocks.note: first meaning: belonging to Emmy, a girl's name
second meaning: the American television industry's annual prizes

explanation.walkthrough: Without the apostrophe, the possessive girl's name is also the plural of the television award.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmys are the US television awards; Emmy's is a girl's name in the possessive.

clue.text: Golden Globe winning actress may make heaviest demand

indicators.note: what the letters may make is something new built out of them, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prize-winning actress might make the heaviest of demands on those around her.
explanation.definitionFit: The British stage and screen actress won a Golden Globe for her role in The Chalk Garden (1964).

clue.text: The Lord of the Flies novelist?

blocks.note: first meaning: Beelzebub, the devil
second meaning: Charles, author of Oliver Twist

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase pointing to William Golding, but 'Lord of the Flies' is Beelzebub, the devil, and 'the dickens' is an old euphemism for the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The devil is euphemistically 'the dickens', and Charles of that surname was a celebrated Victorian novelist.

clue.text: A plank on a ship, perhaps

blocks.note: taken as written
a board is a plank of wood

explanation.surface: A plank set out on a ship, as for walking the plank.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on or in a vessel; 'perhaps' allows for trains and planes too.

clue.text: Uncommonly splendid manure required? Don't despair

indicators.note: uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the letters take an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener is reassured that exceptionally fine manure will save the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil desperandum is the Latin motto meaning 'never despair', from Horace.

clue.text: Film, hidden from view on occasion

blocks.note: a blind corner or bend is one hidden from view
a date is an occasion or appointment

explanation.surface: A film kept out of sight on certain occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: Blind Date is a 1987 comedy with Bruce Willis and Kim Basinger.
explanation.definitionFit: Blind Date is the title of a 1987 Hollywood comedy film, as well as a meeting with a stranger.

clue.text: Caricature of girl in opera, lead in Carmen

indicators.note: the lead is what goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme
opening letter of the opera's name

explanation.surface: A send-up of an operatic heroine, with the star of Carmen in the lead role.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to caricature: to imitate someone in an exaggerated way for comic effect.

clue.text: Essayist is overwhelmed by extra charge

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed by something is to be swamped and surrounded by it

blocks.note: an add-on is an extra item or charge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer is swamped by an unexpected surcharge.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison was the 18th-century English essayist who co-founded The Spectator.

clue.text: Abstemious - tea user, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged in another way

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tea drinker might be the abstemious type who avoids alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere describes a severe, self-denying way of living, close in sense to abstemious.

clue.text: Gloomy day - sail out across mouth of Mersey

indicators.note: out here means out of order, so the letters are rearranged
lying across something means stretching over it on both sides, enclosing it
a river's mouth is at its edge, so only the first letter of the name is used

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for day
taken as written, then rearranged
first letter of the river's name

explanation.surface: A dreary day sailing out across the estuary of the Mersey, the Liverpool river.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal and gloomy are synonyms, both describing dreary, depressing conditions or moods.

clue.text: Pretty girls using extortion in plant

blocks.note: lovelies is a dated term for attractive young women
to bleed someone is to extort money from them

explanation.surface: Attractive young women running an extortion racket from inside a plant, such as a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-lies-bleeding is an amaranth, a garden plant with long drooping crimson flower tassels.

clue.text: Ad lib from retired English politician in shot

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: ex means former, as one who has retired
shot in the sense of raced or tore along
E is the abbreviation for English
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A retired English politician improvises in a film shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means spoken without preparation, exactly what an ad-lib remark is.

clue.text: Warehouse, one pretty nearly bust

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
something bust is broken, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: A warehouse business, one that is pretty nearly bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a warehouse or a port where goods are stored for re-export.

clue.text: See 14
Killer, hideous brute grabbing child

indicators.note: something hideous is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
grabbing means seizing and holding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A murderer, an ugly thug, snatching a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher, figuratively, is a person who kills brutally or indiscriminately.

clue.text: A dry heat out East, all things considered

indicators.note: out means taken away, so one letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation, the letter taken out of heat

explanation.surface: A dry heat out in the East, overall.
explanation.definitionFit: At that is an idiom meaning moreover or when everything is taken into account.

clue.text: Row about Diane being neater

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
Di is the short form of Diane

explanation.surface: A quarrel about Diane being tidier than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidier and neater are comparative synonyms, both meaning more orderly.

clue.text: Copper getting a cut climbing dome

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the letters are read from the bottom up

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
taken as written
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A police officer with a pay cut climbs a dome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola is a small rounded dome on a roof.

clue.text: Master in pain through most of term

indicators.note: going through something means sitting inside it
most of means not all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster suffering through most of the school term.
explanation.definitionFit: A master, in British school usage, is a male schoolteacher.

clue.text: Tennis champion served up nine after holding initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used
in a down clue, sent up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: first letter of the word
taken as written, then turned upwards

explanation.surface: A tennis champion served nine aces after holding serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' sounds like tennis but signals the upward reading in a down clue; 'after' puts the turned piece behind the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Justine Henin of Belgium won seven Grand Slam singles titles and was world number one.

clue.text: Firm not persuaded

blocks.note: first meaning: steady, staying in place
second meaning: not swayed by argument or emotion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, but it is the adjective for something steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmoved describes something fixed in place and someone whose opinion an argument has failed to shift.

clue.text: After hours, a lecturer was wearing

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hours
taken as written
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: After hours, a lecturer was dressed in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you that A and the lecturer come behind the abbreviation for hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something on is to wear it, so had on is the past tense, was wearing.

clue.text: He, say, must stand in front of church to make an announcement

blocks.note: the word he is an example of a pronoun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A man must stand at the front of the church to make an announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a man, but it is the grammatical word; 'must stand in front of' places it before the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to declare formally, as in pronouncing a couple married.

clue.text: Argue in protest about WW1 battle charge after commencement of truce

indicators.note: the commencement is the beginning, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
Mons in Belgium was an early battle of the First World War
first letter of the word
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Protesting about a First World War battle and a charge made after a truce began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the charge behind the first letter of truce.
explanation.definitionFit: To remonstrate is to make a forcefully reproachful protest or argument.
